In summary, our research is concerned with

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
we have improved the sample complexity of PAC-learning by a constant factor, for all concept classes.
our new upper bound is within a factor of at most 2 from the best possible upper bound on the sample complexity for learning in the Haussler-Pollard model.

we have shown that the sample complexity of PAC learning in the realizable case is polynomial in the size of the hypothesis set and the number of relevant features, but exponential in the number of irrelevant features.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown that the sample complexity of PAC learning is within a constant of the best possible.

the sample complexity of the decision theoretic model is within a constant of the best possible, and the sample complexity of PAC learning with respect to VC dimension is within a constant for the class of real-valued functions.
we have improved the sample complexity of PAC learning from $O(\log^{2}n)$ to $O(\log n)$.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in the decision theoretic model, learning can be done with a number of examples that is polynomial in the number of relevant variables.
the sample complexity of a learning problem is determined not only by its complexity, but also by the complexity of the target function.
in many learning scenarios it is sufficient to estimate the expected value of a function on a small number of points.
